::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[. Find the partial fraction decomposition of the following rational function.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1114364/find-the-partial-fraction-decomposition-of-the-following-rational-function), asked by [UltraSound](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/209644/ultrasound) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-22; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Find the PFD of the folowing:
>
> $$\frac{x^6-x^5+48x^3-53x^2+99x+48}{x^5-2x^4+2x^3-4x^2+x-2}$$
> Initially I used long division and got $$x+1+\frac{50(x^3-x^2+2x+1)}{x^5-2x^4+2x^3-4x^2+x-2}$$ I then used trial and error to factor the denominator as:
> $$x+1+\frac{50(x^3-x^2+2x+1)}{x^5-2x^4+2x^3-4x^2+x-2}=x+1+\frac{50(x^3-x^2+2x+1)}{(x-2)(x^4+2x^2+1)}$$
> How do I factor the second part of the denominator?
:::

The second part of the denominator factors as
$$(x^4 + 2x^2 + 1) = ((x^2)^2 + 2(x^2) + 1) = (x^2 + 1)^2$$
Therefore, your partial fraction decomposition is of the form
$$\frac{A}{x-2} + \frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1} + \frac{Dx+E}{(x^2+1)^2}$$
